It is called dark humour.

When you enjoy someone's come uppance, it is dark humour. There is suffering, but it is earned suffering.

It is called schadenfreude, and some confuse it with being amused by someone else's suffering. That is not schadenfreude, schadenfreude is enjoying someone else's suffering after they earned that suffering.

When the bad guy falls into a pit of lava, when the thief in the movie is caught by the roving monster, when the douchebag corporate tool who has been an antagonist gets fired... That is schadenfreude.

This is schadenfreude, and it is a dark humour.

There's a difference between schadenfreude and black comedy, and black comedy is an art that most lack. It requires subtely to be funny. This has the subtlety of an ax.

edit: black comedy is not laughing at someone's come uppance (sic), it's laughing at tragedy. The thing about tragedy is that it is undeserved. It is absurd. Tragedy has no conscience. It visits us all, good and bad. That's why we can all laugh at it.

There is an overlap, a Venn diagram would be of use in this case.

Any dark humour involves suffering, but schadenfreude is the dark humour where the bad guy falls into the hands of the Mummy.

And there is never a need to be subtle - not for any kind of humour, it just needs to get a laugh.

A wry, dark laugh is still a laugh.
